newsitem.title: USA: Rimson fined $9.5 million, broker registration revoked.
newsitem.headline: Rimson fined $9.5 million, broker registration revoked.

text.p: An administrative law judge Wednesday ordered brokerage M. Rimson & Co. Inc. to pay a $9.5 million civil penalty for allegedly using high pressure and fraudulent sales tactics.
Lillian McEwen, a Securities and Exchange Commission judge, also ordered the broker-dealer registration of the New York-based company be revoked.
McEwen issued a cease and desist order and ordered Rimson & Co. barred from being associated with a member of a national securities exchange or registered securities association.
Under SEC rules, the respondents have 21 days after they receive a copy of the judgment to petition for a review, otherwise it will become final.

McEwen ordered Moshe Rimson and Alex David Shindman barred from being associated with a broker or dealer, as well as with a member of a national securities exchange or registered securities association, and from participating in offerings of so-called penny stocks.

Rimson, 68, the company's president and sole shareholder, was ordered to pay a civil penalty of $1.9 million while Shindman, 29, was ordered to pay a $400,000 civil penalty and pay back $2,848.13 in ill-gotten profits plus prejudgement interest. Shindman supervised a group of salesman working at Rimson.
Rimson and Rimson & Co. also were ordered jointly to pay back $730,000 in ill-gotten profits plus prejudgement interest, the SEC said.
McEwen found that Rimson, a broker-dealer registered with the Commission since June 3, 1970, allowed unregistered salesmen to operate so-called "boiler rooms."

The boiler room operation consisted of 30 unregistered salesmen selling speculative securities using sales practices that included material misrepresentations and omissions. The National Association of Securities Dealers expelled Rimson & Co. on Aug. 10, 1995.
